### Town of Nottingham

- **Type:** Town
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** Planning Board voted 5-0-0 on 2026-07-01 to adopt and advance the proposed ordinance; Nottingham voters ratified it at a September 8, 2026 special town election (held with the state primary) by a vote of 1,335 to 143, per the town's official election results.
- **Normalized date:** `2026-09-08` (exact)
- **Duration:** Twelve months from adoption by the legislative body, unless repealed earlier; NHPR reports voter approval on September 8, 2026. The exact operative start and end dates remain unverified.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `nh-town-of-nottingham-undated`
- **Legal basis:** The earlier inventory attributes a 5-0-0 Planning Board vote on July 1, 2026 to adopt and advance a temporary data-center moratorium under RSA 674:23. NHPR reports voter approval 1,335-143 on September 8, 2026. The town-hosted ordinance states that it takes effect upon adoption by the legislative body and lasts twelve months from adoption unless repealed earlier; the ordinance PDF does not certify the vote or establish later force.
- **What prompted it:** Local opposition to a withdrawn Nottingham Business Park data center concept (145 Old Turnpike Road) and an online petition that drew more than 25,000 signatures
- **Affected projects:** Would apply townwide to data center applications, including any resubmission of the withdrawn Nottingham Business Park (145 Old Turnpike Road) concept.
- **Detailed status:** NHPR reports September 8, 2026 voter approval of the twelve-month data-center moratorium, 1,335 yes to 143 no. The town-hosted sample ballot bears the same handwritten totals and twelve-month wording; no explicit result certification statement is supplied on that page. The town-hosted ordinance provides for effectiveness upon legislative-body adoption and twelve months from adoption unless repealed earlier. Later action and current legal force remain unresolved. [VERIFY: later amendments/extensions/repeal, judicial developments and current legal force.]
- **Outcome:** Nottingham voters approved the proposed 12-month data-center moratorium at the September 8, 2026 special town election, 1,335 to 143, according to NHPR.

### HB1265 (2026, LSR 26-2482)

- **Policy ID:** `nh-hb1265-2026-lsr-26-2482`
- **Sponsor / party:** Reps. Peter Schmidt, Wendy Thomas, Tony Caplan; D
- **Recorded status:** Killed in House (Inexpedient to Legislate adopted on House floor), 2026-03-11; Commerce and Consumer Affairs committee reported Inexpedient to Legislate 2026-02-18, vote 15-0
- **Provisions:** Introduced HB1265 would prohibit beginning construction of a new data center from the act’s effective date through one year following, and create a study committee on environmental impacts. The introduced act proposes effectiveness 60 days after passage; the one-year construction interval is anchored to that effective date, not enactment. No operative moratorium or actual effective/end date is asserted for this failed proposal.
- **Mechanism / scope:** statewide_moratorium; statewide
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://gc.nh.gov/bill_status/billinfo.aspx?id=1685&inflect=2>)

### HB1722 (2026, LSR 26-2682)

- **Policy ID:** `nh-hb1722-2026-lsr-26-2682`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Kat McGhee; Rep. Tony Caplan; Rep. Wendy Thomas; Sen. Rebecca Perkins Kwoka; D
- **Recorded status:** Killed in House (Inexpedient to Legislate adopted 185-156 after a special order motion passed 214-126), 2026-03-12; Science, Technology and Energy committee reported Inexpedient to Legislate 2026-02-17, vote 10-8 (minority: Ought to Pass)
- **Provisions:** Introduced HB1722 would create RSA chapter 374-I for facilities that both can use at least 20 MW at peak demand and are primarily engaged in NAICS 518210 services, including computer processing, data processing centers and web hosting. It proposes a separate PUC retail-service class and tariff, cost-allocation/ratepayer protections, minimum 10-year service contracts with billing and termination protections, and an initial tariff docket by January 1, 2028. These are proposed obligations, not operative tariffs.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; unknown
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://gc.nh.gov/bill_status/billinfo.aspx?id=1892&inflect=2>)

### HB1724 (2026, LSR 26-2735)

- **Policy ID:** `nh-hb1724-2026-lsr-26-2735`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Wendy Thomas; D
- **Recorded status:** Official docket labels HB1724 DIED, SESSION ENDED; last listed committee action is February 17, 2026 (Science, Technology and Energy majority report Inexpedient to Legislate 10–8, minority Ought to Pass with Amendment 2026-0737h). The June 4 House journal records adjournment to the call of the chair; no exact final sine-die date is asserted from that journal.
- **Provisions:** Would require annual utility reporting on transmission, wholesale market, capacity, and generation adequacy. The introduced text specifically requires analysis of anticipated generation capacity needs for data centers requiring 5 MW or more and recommendations to insulate ratepayers from interconnection, transmission, rate structure, and stranded-cost risks.

- **Policy ID:** `nh-hb1739-fn-2026-lsr-26-2699`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Santosh Salvi et al.; Sen. Kevin Avard; Mixed (Salvi and other House sponsors are D; Avard is R, as listed in the official bill docket).
- **Recorded status:** Killed in House (Inexpedient to Legislate adopted by voice vote), 2026-02-19; Science, Technology and Energy committee reported Inexpedient to Legislate 2026-02-03, vote 18-0
- **Provisions:** Introduced HB1739 would create RSA chapter 162-V for large-scale data-center campuses, with municipal property-tax stabilization or PILOT agreements, transferable business-tax credits, grid modernization agreements and cost-sharing/non-gas generation procurement, fast-track industrial/brownfield siting, host-community agreements, noise/setbacks, resident bill credits and workforce provisions. The credit text states a percentage of construction costs subject to a statewide cap of 20 percent of total construction costs. The appended fiscal note flags ambiguity in the credit/cap, tax interactions and administration; a fixed 20 percent per-project entitlement is not established. No proposed incentive or obligation is asserted as enacted.

### HB672-FN (2025, LSR 25-0365) -> Chapter 285

- **Policy ID:** `nh-hb672-fn-2025-lsr-25-0365-chapter-285`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Michael Vose et al.; Sens. Timothy Lang, Howard Pearl, David Watters; Mixed (Vose, Lang, Pearl are R; Watters is D)
- **Recorded status:** Enacted as Chapter 285, signed by Governor Ayotte 2025-08-01, effective 2025-08-01
- **Provisions:** Created RSA 374:3-c for qualifying off-grid electricity providers that begin operations on or after August 1, 2025, exempting them from RSA Title XXXIV while they meet statutory conditions; other applicable laws remain in force. The law is not a data center moratorium, but secondary sources describe it as a possible pathway for energy-intensive users such as data centers.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; utility_grid

- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://gc.nh.gov/bill_status/legacy/bs2016/billText.aspx?id=372&sy=2025&txtFormat=html>)

### SB439 (2026, LSR 26-2236)

- **Policy ID:** `nh-sb439-2026-lsr-26-2236`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Debra Altschiller; Rep. Hope Damon; D
- **Recorded status:** Died on table, session ended 2026-08-19; House laid on the table 2026-05-14, 304-11 (following House Municipal and County Government majority report Ought to Pass with Amendment #2026-1807h, 11-9, on 2026-05-05; minority report Inexpedient to Legislate); Senate passed with amendment 2026-01-29, 16-8
- **Provisions:** Introduced SB439 would add RSA 674:81–84, with a 10 percent on-site enterprise-computing exclusion, discretionary municipal permitting in commercial/industrial zones, and utility-capacity, transit-separation, noise and design/siting conditions. The Senate-amended January 29, 2026/0176s text instead proposes RSA 674:81–83, a 25 percent on-site exclusion, data centers allowed in commercial/industrial districts subject to local land-use regulations, and planning-board rulemaking with local legislative-body approval. The compared Senate text omits the introduced prescriptive utility/noise/siting clauses. These are distinct proposed versions, not enacted zoning rights; the later House proposed amendment is not treated as adopted.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; local_government
- **Legal effect:** failed
